quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q1 2026 (December quarter): revenue came in above guidance and revenue and earnings were above expectations, as management said demand is improving "at a faster and stronger pace than previously expected." Gross margin was 49.6% (helped by customer/product mix and revenue on systems previously expensed through prior impairment charges and R&D), GAAP EPS $0.32 and non-GAAP EPS $0.44; total operating expense was $81.1 million GAAP and $74.2 million non-GAAP, and tax expense was $5.7 million. By end market: general semiconductor revenue rose 27% sequentially and over 90% year over year, with all reportable segments up sequentially in general semiconductor; memory demand declined sequentially due to product and customer mix after a 60% increase the prior quarter; automotive and industrial improved 15% sequentially, though industry headwinds are expected to linger through fiscal 2026; aftermarket products and services rose 14% year over year.
quarterly_data.figure: gross margin 49.6%; GAAP EPS $0.32, non-GAAP EPS $0.44; general semiconductor revenue +27% QoQ and over 90% YoY; automotive and industrial +15% QoQ

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance: for the March quarter K&S expected revenue to increase 15% sequentially to $230 million with gross margin of 49%, non-GAAP operating expenses of $73 million, GAAP EPS of $0.53 and non-GAAP EPS of $0.67. Beyond that, Lester Wong (interim CEO and CFO) said Q3 "definitely will be sequentially better than Q2" and that "the second half of FY '26 should be about 15% to 20% better than the first half", calling that the visibility he has today with possible upside. He expected gross margin for the rest of FY '26 to be around 49% to 50% (the long-standing target is 50%), helped by more demand for higher-margin high-performance ball bonders and by volume absorption.
quarterly_data.figure: March quarter guide: revenue +15% QoQ to $230 million, gross margin 49%, GAAP EPS $0.53, non-GAAP EPS $0.67; second half of FY '26 about 15% to 20% better than the first half

quarterly_data.signal: Demand and utilisation: management reported improving order activity with additional visibility through fiscal 2026. General semiconductor utilisation is estimated to remain over 80%, and ball bonding utilisation in the memory market exceeds 85%, up from the mid-70% range last year, which management read as a healthy capacity environment for its NAND assembly solutions; it added "While AI-related workloads are driving capacity tightness across the memory market", they are also driving new packaging for cost-effective stacked DRAM and emerging high-bandwidth flash (HBF). By region: China is over 90%, the rest of Asia around 80%, Southeast Asia still in the 70% range but rising, North America over 80% and North America plus Europe about 80%. Lester Wong said "data center is basically the central driver for this cycle": K&S has been taking share in leading-edge logic for data centers, is already in production for some of the most advanced heterogeneous logic applications, its core ball bonders serve data-center infrastructure, networking, communication, power and storage chips, and enterprise SSD use in data centers is also helping the memory business.
quarterly_data.figure: general semiconductor utilisation over 80%; memory ball bonding utilisation exceeds 85% (up from the mid-70% range last year); China over 90%

quarterly_data.signal: HBM: K&S extended its thermo-compression (TCB) footprint into high-bandwidth memory and shipped its first HBM system to a large memory customer during the December quarter; the system went to the customer's facility in the U.S. and is undergoing qualification. The next milestone is hopefully another system shipment; "There may be POs within FY '26, but I think actual production would be more FY '27" and "I think volume production will be in fiscal '27." Management continues to anticipate "Fluxless thermocompression remain a strong alternative to hybrid bonding for the next-generation HBM needs."
quarterly_data.figure: first HBM system shipped in the December quarter, in qualification; volume production expected in fiscal '27

quarterly_data.signal: High-bandwidth flash (HBF): asked whether HBF is a TCB or vertical-wire opportunity, Lester Wong said "it is a TCB play, not for vertical wire" (probably the APTURA tool). HBF is designed to merge NAND-level capacity with HBM-class performance and targets to match HBM bandwidth with 8 to 16x capacity; it is still in early stages, multiple packaging technologies may be used, and K&S is exploring it with a few customers. The next milestone would probably be shipping a system before a PO, and commercial timing is "probably be more of a CY '27 play."
quarterly_data.figure: HBF targets 8 to 16x capacity at HBM bandwidth; expected to be more of a CY '27 play

quarterly_data.signal: Vertical wire (K&S says it pioneered the technology) is its other DRAM opportunity, a cost-effective die-stacking alternative for bandwidth; customer feedback is positive and management anticipates strong sequential growth in both TCB and vertical wire over the coming years. It is gaining traction with some volume possibly in the latter half of FY '26 but expanding much more in FY '27; "We're currently working with 8 customers in Korea, China and the U.S. on this." Together with the HBM system shipped to the leading memory maker, this is K&S's move from its traditionally NAND-heavy memory business into DRAM.
quarterly_data.figure: vertical wire: working with 8 customers in Korea, China and the U.S.; expanding much more in FY '27

quarterly_data.signal: TCB installed base and capacity: "We have 120 TCBs in the field, and half of those are Fluxless." K&S's TCB business started with an IDM in the U.S., moved on to foundry, and is now seeing "quite a lot of demand from OSAT"; advanced TCB capacity is in demand throughout the customer base and the Advanced Solutions segment is expected to grow strongly this year. The formic-acid Fluxless TCB (FTC) is already qualified and in high-volume production, while qualification of the plasma FTC version is under way with a customer. K&S is expanding its Singapore facility "to increase our Fluxless thermocompression production capacity by 3x."
quarterly_data.figure: 120 TCBs in the field, half Fluxless; Singapore expansion to increase Fluxless TCB production capacity by 3x
